AnalyzeRequest.description:
Request body for the analyze endpoint.

Usually the page itself (``page_content`` and/or ``page_facts``). A request with only a ``url`` has the server
fetch the page: one it can't read (an error, a bot check, a page that needs a browser) is refused before any
charge.

checkout_content.description: HTML of the checkout page for this product, if available, to detect fees added at checkout.
checkout_content.title: Checkout Content

flags.description: Names of optional skills to activate in addition to the default set.
flags.title: Flags

page_content.description: Raw HTML, or the page's cleaned main text when page_facts is supplied.
page_content.title: Page Content

page_facts.description: Facts extracted from the rendered page (e.g. by the browser extension). When absent, the server extracts them from page_content.

proof_of_work.description: A free deep check (no pass, or a pass without bought checks): a solved challenge from GET /v1/analyze/challenge, used once. Not needed for a quick check or a deep check a pass pays for.

tier.description: deep (the default): the full analysis, which uses a check. quick: rule-based checks of the page itself only (no LLM, no lookups elsewhere; product pages), free for everyone and never charged.
tier.title: Tier

url.description: URL of the product page. Sent alone (no page_content or page_facts), the server fetches it.
url.title: Url

The count is left out when it isn't known (a free check without a pass).

For agents: `/llms.txt`.
info.title: Unfret API

post.description:
Analyse a product web page: free for shoppers, or paid from a pass's bought checks.

Passes the page (client-supplied facts and/or HTML or cleaned text) through the graph, which extracts the
facts, runs the cheap skills in parallel, lets the triage decide on expensive ones, then synthesises a
reliability score, an explanation and the shopper verdict (in English).

**Free (shoppers: the extension, the app, the link checker).** Send no ``Authorization``. ``"tier": "quick"``
(rules only) needs nothing else, a few a minute. A deep check (the default tier) needs a solved challenge from
``GET /v1/analyze/challenge`` as ``proof_of_work`` (428 ``PROOF_OF_WORK_REQUIRED`` without one, 400
``BAD_CHALLENGE`` for a bad one), at most ``free_deep_checks_per_ip_per_hour`` per network (429
``TOO_MANY_REQUESTS``). Once the free pool (or the day's limit on it) is used up, free deep checks are refused
with 429 ``FREE_CHECKS_PAUSED`` (``metadata``: ``reason`` ``spend_ceiling``, ``scope`` ``day``, ``retry_after_s``,
``quick_checks``, ``message_key`` ``free_checks_run_on_donations``, ``donate_url``) until 00:00 UTC. Nothing ties a
free check to anyone: it carries no ``report_token``.

**Paid (a pass or wallet with bought checks).** ``Authorization: Bearer ufk_…`` (or a wallet's session): a deep
check uses one bought check, taken up front and given back when the page can't be analysed (score -1) or the
analysis fails. A pass without bought checks is not used: its deep check is a free one (needs ``proof_of_work``).
The same input analysed again within the hour costs a paying account a check like a fresh analysis, except for
the account that already paid for that page within the hour.

Nothing about the page or the result is stored; the ``report_token`` (a paying account's or a quick check's with
an account) lets the caller report a wrong result later (``POST /v1/reports``); the ``share_token`` lets anyone
who has the result make it public as a link (``POST /v1/shares``, without any account).

A request with only a ``url`` has the server fetch the page first (the web link checker). A page it can't check
that way is answered with a free 422: ``PAGE_UNAVAILABLE`` (couldn't be fetched), ``PAGE_BLOCKED`` (the shop
refuses automatic visitors, or answered with a bot check), ``PAGE_TOO_THIN`` (an empty shell that needs a
browser) or ``INVALID_URL``.

:param body: The request body containing the page content and flags.
:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the compiled graph).
:param account: The account (injected by optional_account), or ``None`` without ``Authorization`` (only a quick
    check may do without one).
:return: Reliability score (0–100), explanation, verdict, the scorer's assessment, the balance left, a report
    token and a share token.
:raises InternalServerError: If the graph fails.
:raises GatewayTimeoutError: If the analysis takes longer than ``analysis_timeout_s``.
:raises asyncio.CancelledError: If the client hung up (after the refund).

get.description:
A proof-of-work challenge for a free deep check: solve it, then send it with the check as ``proof_of_work``.

Find a ``solution`` (at most 32 characters, e.g. a decimal counter) with ``SHA-256(challenge + ":" + solution)``
starting with ``bits`` zero bits. Each challenge works once, until ``expires_at``. It names nothing: no client,
network or page. While the month's free deep checks are paused (``paused``: the LLM spend ceiling), don't solve
it: the check would be refused with 429 ``FREE_CHECKS_PAUSED``; ``paused_until`` and the rest say why and what to
show (``message_key``, ``donate_url``). Quick checks need no challenge.

:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The challenge, its difficulty and expiry, and whether free deep checks are paused.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While free deep checks can't be offered.

post.description:
Analyse a page like ``POST /v1/analyze``, streaming progress as server-sent events while skills finish.

Events: one ``step`` per finished node (``{"skill", "findings", "check"}`` with the finding types and whether the
step is one of the checks the result's ``checks_run`` counts, plus ``page_type`` once classified), then a final
``result`` (the ``POST /v1/analyze`` body, with all the evidence) or ``error``.
Charged like ``POST /v1/analyze`` (a cache hit's result comes at once, charged as there), refunded on ``error``,
a score of -1, or when the client hangs up before the analysis finished. A finished result is cached first, so a
client that lost the connection gets it again for free by repeating the request with the same account. A
URL-only request fetches the page before the stream starts; a page that can't be checked is a free 422 (no
stream), as for ``POST /v1/analyze``.
Free checks (``proof_of_work``, the spend ceiling) and ``"tier": "quick"`` work as for ``POST /v1/analyze``.

:param body: The request body containing the page content and flags.
:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the compiled graph).
:param account: The account (injected by optional_account), or ``None`` without ``Authorization``.
:return: A ``text/event-stream`` response.

post.description:
Check a store or product page for scam, dropshipping and dark-pattern signals, with an Unfret pass or x402.

**With a pass** (``Authorization: Bearer ufk_…``; a developer pass from ``GET /v1/keys/challenge?developer=true``
and ``POST /v1/keys``): a deep check uses one of the pass's checks, free ones first; a quick check is free. The
verdict adds ``charged``, ``free_check``, ``balance_usd_micros`` and ``free_checks_left``. **With x402** (no
account): without a payment or a pass the answer is 402 with the options in ``PAYMENT-REQUIRED`` (USDC and wSOL on
Solana, and USDC on Base where it is on: ``/.well-known/x402`` lists them); pay one and send the request again
with ``PAYMENT-SIGNATURE``. Retrying with the same payment returns the same answer (for 15 minutes) and is never
charged twice. The 402 comes whatever the body; the body is validated (422) only with a payment or a pass. Every
error is JSON with ``detail`` and ``error_code`` (``/llms.txt`` lists them, and whether each was charged).

:param body: URL, optional page HTML, tier and policy.
:param request: The incoming request (payment header or pass, app state).
:return: The verdict, or an x402 payment-required / error response.

401.description: Not a valid Unfret pass (only with Authorization): INVALID_API_KEY

402.description: Payment required (x402: the options are in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header), a refused payment, or the pass has no checks left (INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS)

422.description: An invalid body, or a page Unfret couldn't fetch (PAGE_UNAVAILABLE, PAGE_BLOCKED)

503.description: Payments or the analysis are off for a moment: retry after Retry-After

504.description: The analysis timed out: not charged (x402 on Solana: credited to the paying wallet)

post.description:
Start a card (or other fiat) payment for a pack that tops up an API key, at the provider's hosted checkout.

The provider is the seller: it handles the buyer's details, invoice and sales tax/VAT; this service only learns
that the key was paid for. Credited the pack's value when the provider's webhook confirms the payment.

In euros for ``currency: "eur"`` (by default for visitors from the euro area), in dollars otherwise. A local
payment method (``payment_method``, e.g. ``wero``) is a checkout in its currency with its billing country
prefilled, which is what makes the provider show it. Should the provider refuse a euro checkout (e.g. a product
without its euro price yet), the buyer gets the dollar card checkout instead of none; ``currency`` and
``payment_method`` in the response say which it is.

:param body: The key, the pack, the currency and the payment method.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The checkout URL.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While no fiat provider is configured, or it can't start a checkout.
:raises BadRequestError: For euros while euro prices are off, or a method in another currency than asked for.

get.description:
Whether a card checkout has been paid: for the checkout page on the way back.

Needs the checkout's claim token (``X-Unfret-Claim``, from ``fiat-checkout``): the provider knows the checkout's
id, but never the token. 404 for an unknown checkout, a wrong or missing token, or one older than a month.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param response: The response (marked uncacheable: it changes once paid).
:param checkout_id: The checkout's id (from ``fiat-checkout``).
:param x_unfret_claim: The checkout's claim token.
:return: Paid or not, and the pack size.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While card payments are off.
:raises UnknownCheckoutError: For an unknown checkout or a wrong or missing claim token.

post.description:
Pick up a card purchase in another browser: a fresh pass (API key) for the key it paid for.

For a buyer whose bank app or phone brought them back to a browser without the pass that was made for the
purchase. The provider's return link names the checkout (``/checkout?paid=1&checkout=<id>``). Allowed once,
within 24 hours of the payment, and only while the browser that paid hasn't picked the purchase up itself (a
status poll with its claim token after payment); the key is rotated: a new key and recovery code, the same id
and balance, and the old key stops working. Only for a pass made for the purchase: a top-up of a pass that had
checks before (or got some since, from another card order) is never rotated from here.

Refusals: 404 ``UNKNOWN_CHECKOUT``; 409 ``CHECKOUT_NOT_PAID`` (not confirmed yet: retry after a few seconds);
409 ``CHECKOUT_TOPPED_UP`` (the checks went to a pass in use: nothing to collect here); 409
``CHECKOUT_COLLECTED`` (picked up already); 410 ``CHECKOUT_EXPIRED``; 429 (too many attempts from here).

:param request: The incoming request.
:param response: The response (marked uncacheable).
:param checkout_id: The checkout's id, from the return link.
:return: The new pass, shown this once.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While card payments are off.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: If this network tried too many times today.
:raises UnknownCheckoutError: For an unknown checkout.
:raises CheckoutNotPaidError: While the payment isn't confirmed.
:raises CheckoutToppedUpError: When the purchase topped up a pass in use.
:raises CheckoutCollectedError: When the purchase was picked up already.
:raises CheckoutExpiredError: After the window.

Build the unsigned SOL or USDC transfer that buys a pack of credits; the buyer's wallet signs and sends it.

The pack costs its crypto price, VAT included: the buyer's country (see ``vat`` in ``/v1/pricing``) only decides
how much of it is VAT. The transaction's memo names the stored quote. Credits arrive once the transfer is finalized
(about 15–30 seconds): everything that arrived, credited to the paying wallet unless ``beneficiary`` or ``key_id``
says otherwise.
No sign-in needed: anyone may fund any wallet or API key.

:param body: Which pack, for whom, paid how, from where.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The transaction (base64), a Solana Pay link for phone wallets, and the price breakdown.

get.description:
Whether a purchase has been paid: for the checkout to show when the checks have arrived.

No sign-in: the quote's id (from ``purchase-tx`` or the QR code's ``X-Unfret-Quote`` header) is random, so only
whoever started the purchase knows it until the payment's memo puts it on chain, which shows as much already.
Says nothing about who pays or who gets the checks. Quotes are deleted a day after they expire (404 then).

:param request: The incoming request.
:param response: The response (marked uncacheable: it changes once paid).
:param quote_id: The quote's id.
:return: Paid or not, and the pack size.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: Without a database.
:raises UnknownQuoteError: For an unknown, expired or malformed id.

The Solana Pay request for a pack as a QR code, for paying from a phone wallet.

The price (VAT included) and its breakdown are in the ``X-Unfret-Total-Usd`` and ``X-Unfret-Vat-Rate``
headers; the quote's id, to poll ``/v1/credits/quotes/{quote_id}`` with, in ``X-Unfret-Quote``; the Solana Pay
link itself (to open a wallet app on the same phone) in ``X-Unfret-Pay-Url``.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param checks: The pack size.
:param country: The buyer's country (ISO 3166 alpha-2), for VAT.
:param currency: ``SOL`` or ``USDC``.
:param beneficiary: The wallet to credit; without it the paying wallet is credited.
:param key_id: The API key to credit instead.
:return: An SVG image.

Liveness probe. Always returns 200 while the process is serving requests.

:return: Healthy response with the running version, the commit it was built from and the scorers' versions.

Readiness probe. Returns 200 only while the database answers, so a deploy can wait for it.

Also reports whether x402 payments and card top-ups are available and how many alerts are raised; with the
operator token (``Authorization: Bearer``), the hot wallet's balances and the alerts themselves. A low balance or
a compromise signal pauses payments (``/v1/check`` answers 503) but never fails readiness: the rest of the API
keeps serving.

:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the DB pool).
:return: Healthy response with the running version and commit.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: If the database pool is missing or the query fails.

A small JPEG of a photo in the image index (the thumbnails in photo findings point here).

:param request: The incoming request (its visitor network, for the limit).
:param print_id: The index row, from a finding's thumbnail URL.
:return: The JPEG, cacheable for a day.
:raises HTTPException: 404 for an unknown row or a photo that is gone.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: Over the thumbnails allowed from this visitor network in a minute.

post.description:
Create an empty API key with a solved challenge; a few per visitor network per day.

400 ``BAD_CHALLENGE`` if the challenge is invalid, expired, used or unsolved; 429 if this network created too many
keys today.

:param body: The solved challenge.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The key and recovery code, shown this once.

get.description:
A proof-of-work challenge for ``POST /v1/keys``: a few seconds of hashing in a browser, used once.

With ``?developer=true``, the challenge a developer pass needs: ``developer_pow_extra_bits`` harder (16 times the
work at the default 4). A developer pass is for trying Unfret out: one per network a day.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param developer: Ask for a developer pass's challenge.
:return: The challenge.

post.description:
Deprecated: always moves nothing.

A shopper's pass no longer has free checks (deep checks are free without a pass), and a developer pass's never
moved. Kept so older extensions get an answer.

:param body: The other pass.
:param request: The incoming request.
:param account: The account (injected by require_account).
:return: How many moved.
:raises BadRequestError: For a wallet's session, or a malformed pass id.

get.description:
A QR code that puts this key on a phone: in the Unfret app when it's installed, else in the link checker.

For a shopper who bought checks in one browser and wants them on their phone. The code holds
``<site>/pass#pass=<key>``: the key is in the fragment, which a browser never sends anywhere. On Android with the
app installed the link opens the app (a verified App Link, :mod:`unfret.android_app_links`); anywhere else
``/pass`` forwards to ``/check`` with the fragment, which asks before it keeps the key like a pasted one and clears
the address bar. Only for an API key (send it as ``Authorization: Bearer``); anyone who scans the code can use the
key's checks, so pages show it only on request.

:param request: The incoming request (its ``Authorization`` header is the key).
:param account: The account (injected by require_account).
:return: The SVG, never cached.
:raises BadRequestError: For a wallet's session: a wallet signs in on the phone itself.

post.description:
Replace a lost key: a new key and a new recovery code, the same id and balance. The old key and code stop working.

:param body: The recovery code.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The new key and recovery code, shown this once.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: If this network tried too many recoveries today.
:raises UnauthorizedError: If the code is not (any longer) valid.

Report a wrong result: the level you think is right, and which findings are wrong or missing.

Send the result's ``label_token`` back with the analysed request exactly as it was sent: the report keeps that
page (scrubbed of personal details) for review, never who sent it. Reports never change a result; reviewed and
agreeing reports become training data. Without a contributor key a report is anonymous, weighs little and counts
only where others agree; one per result. With a key: one per page (a new one replaces the old), 50 a day, and
points on the leaderboard (opt-in).

:param body: The report.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: What happened.
:raises crowd.LabelError: (as an HTTP error) a token for another page.

Object to a result, ask for a correction, or ask Unfret to remove what it keeps about a site or contact detail.

No sign-in. Stored as sent (the site without anything after ``?`` or ``#``), with the day; no IP address or time.
Deleted once handled, or after 90 days. 5 requests per visitor network per day.

:param body: The request.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: That it was received.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: Over today's limit.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: Without a database, or with a full queue.
:raises ObjectionRefusedError: When the site or the reply address isn't one.

get.description:
The price of a check and everything derived from it.

The x402 tiers, the packs (by card in dollars and euros, and the lower crypto price), which countries pay by card
in euros and which have a local payment method, the suggested country and its card currency, the VAT rules for
crypto, exact USDC amounts and a live SOL quote.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param response: The response (marked uncacheable: it carries the visitor's likely country).
:return: The price list.

schema.title: Response Get Pricing V1 Pricing Get

post.description:
Report that a result is wrong (the older form of ``POST /v1/labels``; new clients use that).

Send back the ``report_token`` from the result with the request and explanation exactly as they were, so the
report provably concerns that check (for a URL-only check, the page is fetched again now). The report keeps the
page, scrubbed of personal details, never who sent it. A page already in the queue counts the report as
confirmation; a page reviewed recently is ``already_known``. One report per result.

:param body: The report.
:param request: The incoming request.
:param account: The account the result was for (only to check the token).
:return: The outcome.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: If reports are off (no session secret).

get.description:
The JSON schema of ``PageFacts``, for clients (the browser extension) that extract facts themselves.

:return: The schema.

schema.title: Response Page Facts Schema V1 Schema Page Facts Get

post.description:
Make a result public as a link: ``/r/<id>``, for 90 days. Send it without Authorization; it names no account.

The token must match the url and the result exactly (a share can only show a verdict Unfret gave for that page)
and be under 7 days old. What is stored is what the preview shows: the verdict in public wording (no
score, never "scam" or "fraud"), the product's title and link, the shop and the day of the check; no quotes from
the page and nothing about who checked. A check that included checkout_content can't be shared. 20 shares per
visitor network per day.

:param body: The share token, the checked url and the result.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The id, the link and the delete code (shown this once).
:raises TooManyRequestsError: Over today's limit.

Exactly what ``POST /v1/shares`` would make public, without storing anything. Send it without Authorization.

:param body: The share token, the checked url and the result.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The public fields and the notice to show the sharer.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: Over 30 previews a minute from one visitor network.

delete.description:
Delete a shared result with its delete code (X-Delete-Code), for good.

:param share_id: The share.
:param request: The incoming request.
:param x_delete_code: The delete code shown when it was shared.
:return: 204.
:raises BadRequestError: Without the code.
:raises ForbiddenError: With a wrong code.
:raises NotFoundError: For no such share.

get.description:
A shared result: what a shopper's check of a product page showed that day.

:param share_id: The share.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The shared result (404 once deleted, expired or hidden after an objection).

post.description:
Object to a shared result (a shop owner): it is hidden at once, and Unfret reviews it.

:param share_id: The share.
:param body: Why, optionally.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: ``{"hidden": true}``.
:raises NotFoundError: For no such (visible) share.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: Over today's limit.
